sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美西语近岸软件研发外包与数字客服中心

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Passive Holding of Subsidiary Shares and Corporate Dividends

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Republic of Colombia and the Kingdom of Spain for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (2007)
Free Trade Agreement between Colombia and the United States (entered into force 2012)
Pacific Alliance (Alianza del Pacífico) Framework Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971); Ley 526 de 1999 (creation of UIAF); Ley 1121 de 2006; Ley 1453 de 2011; Ley 2010 de 2019 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales - RUB); Decreto 1960 de 2018; Decreto 830 de 2021; Resolución DIAN 164 de 2021; Circular Básica Jurídica 029 de 2014 de la Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia; Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio Resolution on commercial registry homologation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport of each ultimate beneficial owner and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry or passport office of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Colombia is a party to the 1961 Hague Convention) or, where the issuer is in a non-contracting state, Colombian consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of existence and legal representation (certificado de existencia y representación legal) of the parent holding company, if any
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry / Chamber of Commerce of the jurisdiction of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized corporate resolution authorizing the incorporation and appointing the attorney-in-fact
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public from the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, with sworn Spanish translation where applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Applicants are required to screen every ultimate beneficial owner, director, and signatory against the Colombian Procuraduría General's disciplinary registries, the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia's PEP list, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU/UK sanctions lists, and UIAF AML typologies. Enhanced due diligence applies to PEPs and PEP-associated family members. Negative screening must be documented and retained for a minimum of 10 years. Non-face-to-face clients require additional identification, source-of-funds certification, and heightened documentary due diligence.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) – official portal of Colombian Chambers of Commerce (www.rues.org.co); name clearance is processed electronically through the local Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All statutory corporate names must be registered in Spanish using the international Latin alphabet. The corporate name of a Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada must be followed by the abbreviation 'S.A.S.' or 'SAS'. Names must not consist solely of a generic business activity; a distinctive element is required. Foreign words are accepted if rendered in the Latin alphabet and normally accompanied by a Spanish-language description. Accents and special characters are permitted but must appear identically in all RUES filings and in the deed.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Cámara de Comercio rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file a reconsideration appeal ('recurso de reposición') within 10 business days of notification before the same Cámara de Comercio. If the rejection is upheld, a subsidiary appeal ('recurso de apelación') may be submitted within 5 business days to the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (Delegatura de Superintendencia de Registro Mercantil). The initial name reservation may be extended once for an additional period by filing a new application before expiration, subject to payment of the applicable tariff.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are tolerated for non-operational holding SPVs if the registered address can receive service of process and is not a mere post-office box or mail-forwarding address. For ISIC 6420 passive holding SPVs, virtual offices are generally accepted at initial incorporation; however, enhanced AML due diligence, bank account opening, and tax substance procedures may require a physical in-country presence or a commercial co-working office with dedicated receiving staff.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 20%–35% unannounced physical inspection probability within the first 24-month review cycle; the likelihood increases where the registered address is a virtual office or where annual financial statements indicate inconsistent substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance / homonymy search and reservation certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff set by Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notary fee for preparation and execution of incorporation deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff or prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registration fee at the Chamber of Commerce and filing of UBO data with DIAN

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal fees for pre-incorporation due diligence, UBO piercing, AML/CFT screening, and document review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark / fixed professional fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization fees for foreign corporate and passport documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Colombian consular post
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular tariff and Ministry of Foreign Affairs fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank pre-incorporation account opening and KYC/AML compliance fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank fee schedule and AML compliance cost recovery

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada); Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971) arts. 98-124, 373-381; Ley 222 de 1995; Decreto 1074 de 2015 (RUES registration procedure).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (Registro Único Empresarial - RUES), under the surveillance of the Superintendencia de Sociedades.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation document) with legalized signatures; Escritura Pública is mandatory only if real estate is contributed.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital under Ley 1258 de 2008. The subscribed capital is freely fixed by the incorporators; payment of unpaid subscriptions may be deferred in the bylaws but must be completed within two (2) years from incorporation. No escrow account is required for an S.A.S.; the registration fee and the departmental Impuesto de Registro are calculated on the subscribed capital, with a 0.7% rate applicable once the mayor cuantía threshold is exceeded.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] S.A.S. Adopted unanimously by the sole shareholder on [DATE], in accordance with Law 1258 of 2008. RESOLVED: 1. That the subscribed share capital set forth in the incorporation document be ratified, and the payment schedule for any unpaid subscriptions be approved. 2. That the registered office address, as stated in Article [X] of the bylaws, be formally adopted as the principal place of business. 3. That [NAME] be appointed Legal Representative, and [NAME] be appointed Secretary, each with the powers and duties provided by law and the bylaws. 4. That management take all necessary steps for regulatory registration, including Chamber of Commerce filing, DIAN tax registration, and bank account opening. Certified by the Chairperson.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Search and Homonym Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio - Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) online consultation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed corporate name and a brief description of the corporate purpose through the RUES online consultation module (consulta de nombre). Obtain the certifcado de homónimos confirming that no identical or confusingly similar company is registered. Although an S.A.S. may be constituted without prior reservation, conducting this pre-search minimizes rejection risk and accelerates the subsequent Chamber of Commerce filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and corporate purpose
Personal identification data of the incorporating shareholder(s)
Contact details (email and telephone) of the filing applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the consultation indicates a coincident or confusable name, propose an alternative name containing a distinguishing prefix or suffix and re-run the search; the consultation is free and repeatable online.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Private Incorporation Document (Documento Privado de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary or Cámara de Comercio (autenticación of signatures) with corporate counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución and bylaws in Spanish, including the corporate name, S.A.S. type, registered office address, corporate purpose limited to passive holding of subsidiary shares and receipt of dividends, subscribed and paid capital, a payment schedule for unpaid shares not exceeding two years, appointment of the legal representative, audit and governance clauses, and dispute-resolution provisions. All incorporators must sign the document and legalize their signatures before a notary or an authorized Chamber of Commerce officer. If any contribution consists of real estate, the constitution must be executed as an Escritura Pública before a notary.
required_dossiers: Incorporation document and complete bylaws in Spanish
Copy of the identification document of each incorporator
Capital contribution schedule and payment plan
Appointment acceptance letter of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any inconsistencies identified by the notary or counsel and substitute the corrected document prior to filing; if real estate is contributed, convert the instrument into an Escritura Pública and register the transfer with the Oficina de Registro de Instrumentos Públicos before Chamber filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Registration Tax and Chamber Tariff
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Secretaría de Hacienda of the relevant Department or municipality and financial institutions on the PSE network
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before delivering the incorporation document to the Chamber of Commerce, liquidate and pay the departmental registration tax (Impuesto de Registro) and the Chamber inscription tariff (derechos de inscripción). The registration tax is computed on the subscribed capital under the applicable departmental ordinance, at a rate not exceeding 0.7% once the mayor cuantía threshold is exceeded or at the fixed minimum for minor amounts. Payment is made through the departmental treasury or authorized banking channels; retain the payment voucher for attachment to the Chamber filing.
required_dossiers: Liquidación or pre-payment form generated by the Chamber or treasury
Payment voucher for the Impuesto de Registro
Certificado de homónimos (if obtained)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the treasury identifies an underpayment, pay the difference together with the applicable surcharge; if an overpayment occurs, submit a restitution request before the same tax authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Chamber of Commerce Registration and Matrícula Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio principal of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days following execution of the incorporation document, submit the document together with the Chamber's registration form, the legalized signatures and the payment vouchers. The Chamber verifies compliance with Ley 1258 de 2008, assigns the matrícula mercantil folio, and issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal (C.E.R.L.), which evidences the legal existence and the representational powers of the legal representative. This registration must be completed prior to any DIAN filing.
required_dossiers: Private incorporation document with legalized signatures
Signed Chamber of Commerce registration form (Formulario RUES)
Payment vouchers for the registration tax and the chamber tariff
Homonym certificate when requested by the Chamber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber issues a formal query (requerimiento), remedy the cited defect by filing a corrective clarification within the indicated term, generally ten business days; failure to register within the legal term may expose the company to a fine imposed by the Superintendencia de Sociedades under Article 372 of the Código de Comercio.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: DIAN Tax Registration and NIT Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) - Registro Único Tributario (RUT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the RUT form electronically through the DIAN portal using the data of the C.E.R.L. The DIAN assigns the Número de Identificación Tributaria (NIT). The SPV must declare ISIC code 6420 (activities of holding companies) as its principal activity, adopt the ordinary national tax regime with entity-level taxation, and register, where applicable, for the municipal industry and commerce tax (ICA) with the municipality of the registered office. The legal representative must validate the RUT and subscribe it with the identity data registered at the Chamber.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Copy of the identification document of the legal representative
Completed RUT form with electronic signature
Proof of registered office address if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects the RUT or issues a correction notice due to discrepancies between the Chamber and DIAN databases (for example, address or legal representative mismatch), reconcile the data and resubmit the form; the company's legal existence is not impaired by the RUT rejection provided the constitutional requirements are satisfied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Beneficial Ownership Report (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN - Beneficial Owner Reporting Module (Law 2155 de 2021 and implementing regulations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the initial beneficial owner (beneficiario final) report within 30 calendar days after incorporation, identifying every individual who directly or indirectly owns, controls, or benefits from more than 5% of the shares or who otherwise exercises decisive control, including through the intermediate holding structure. The report must be completed with the full ownership chain of each final beneficiary and must be updated annually or upon any material change.
required_dossiers: Report identifying the final beneficial owners
Ownership chain organigram of the SPV
Supporting constitutional and shareholder documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN issues a notice of incomplete or inconsistent information, correct and refile within the stated deadline; late or inaccurate reporting is subject to fines under Law 2155 de 2021, and the countdown should be monitored from the Chamber registration date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Capital Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank supervised by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate current account in COP and USD suitable for receiving dividend payments and interbank transfers through Swift and traditional rails. Given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier, the bank will apply enhanced due diligence: present the Chamber certificate, RUT, NIT, the approved beneficial owner report, identification and background of the authorized signatories, and a reasonable explanation of projected dividend flows from the operating subsidiaries. After account opening, collect the unpaid portion of subscribed capital according to the bylaws' payment schedule, which may not exceed two years; no escrow account is required.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
RUT and NIT certificates
Bank account application and economic activity profile questionnaire
Beneficial owner declaration and identification documents
Corporate resolution determining authorized signatories
Description of sources of funds and projected dividend flows
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the first bank delays or refuses the application under enhanced compliance requirements, rectify the KYC or UBO documentation and apply to another supervised financial institution; supplement the file with legal counsel's opinion on UBO and source of funds to address heightened due diligence concerns.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Commercial Books (Libros de Comercio)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio - Registro de Libros
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Chamber registration, present the minutes book (libro de actas) and the shareholders register book (libro de registro de accionistas) for Chamber stamping and inscription. Each book must be bound with pre-numbered and authenticated folios; the Chamber records the book folios in the merchant registry, completing the corporate governance infrastructure. From that moment, record shareholder resolutions, minutes and any share transfers chronologically in the registered books.
required_dossiers: Shareholders register book, bound and folio-numbered
Minutes book, bound and folio-numbered
Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Application form for book registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the books fail formal requirements, replace them and re-apply; an adverse finding on book form does not invalidate earlier acts, but late registration of commercial books may lead to formal sanctions from the Superintendencia de Sociedades.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - a pure equity holding SPV under ISIC 6420 requires no industrial license. If administrative premises are later established, the relevant authorities would be the Curaduría Urbana and the municipal planning office (urban permits), together with the Cámara de Comercio (commercial registry).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable. ISIC 6420 (activities of holding companies) is an administrative financial activity, expressly exempt from operating, manufacturing or industrial licensing requirements in Colombia.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) and Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: EIA exempt. The passive holding activity generates no industrial pollution; no environmental license, environmental impact assessment, or prior consultation is required at Stage 2.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the SPV's passive holding activity. If a purely administrative office is later opened, general urban solid waste rules under Decreto 1076 de 2015 apply without EIA; wastewater discharge limits under Resolución 0631 de 2015 and air quality standards under Resolución 2254 de 2017 would arise only from a future industrial transformation project, which is outside the SPV's approved scope.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable at the pure holding stage. If premises are opened, the SPV would obtain: (i) the fire safety inspection certificate from the Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos; (ii) the structural occupancy and sismo-resistencia certificate from the Curaduría Urbana or municipal planning office; and (iii) the occupational health and safety program (SG-SST) with ARL affiliation and the company work regulations (Reglamento de Higiene y Seguridad Industrial) under Resolución 0312 de 2019.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) – National Tax and Customs Directorate, with exclusive competence over income tax, VAT, national consumption tax, customs duties and the single tax registry. Official portal: www.dian.gov.co; all interactions are conducted through the MUISCA electronic services platform (Servicios Informáticos Electrónicos) and the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) module.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly incorporated Colombian S.A.S. used as an equity-holding SPV: (1) execute the incorporation instrument (private document or public deed) before a Colombian notary; (2) obtain the provisional pre-RUT registration from DIAN online before approaching the Chamber of Commerce; (3) file the company in the RUES (Registro Único Empresarial) at the applicable Cámara de Comercio, which transmits the registration data to DIAN; (4) after RUES registration, DIAN assigns the definitive statutory tax identification number (NIT – Número de Identificación Tributaria) and activates the final RUT; (5) appoint and register a legal representative/apoderado; a durable power of attorney, apostilled or consularized, is required for non-resident shareholders; (6) activate the MUISCA account, request the DIAN electronic signature (firma electrónica) and configure the electronic invoicing credentials. The NIT is the exclusive tax ID for all fiscal acts; the RUT is the single-file registration instrument under Article 555-2 of the Colombian Tax Statute (ET), implemented by Decrees 1625 of 2016 and 2153 of 2021.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a Colombian-resident S.A.S. is a separate corporate taxpayer taxed on worldwide income. General corporate income tax headline rate is 35% for FY2024 (Article 240 ET, as amended by Laws 1819/2016 and 2277/2022), with the statutory schedule providing a phased reduction to 33% in the 2025–2027 window; a bank/financial-services surtax applies only to that sector and is irrelevant here. Dividends received from Colombian subsidiaries are statutory non-taxable income for a domestic corporate shareholder (Article 49 ET); foreign-source dividends are taxable with a foreign tax credit; passive foreign investment controlled by the S.A.S. is attributed under the Transparencia Fiscal Internacional (CFC) rules of Article 631 ET. Territorial_Scope: Colombian-source income of non-resident shareholders (dividends, interest, royalties, gains on Colombian shares) is subject to withholding taxation at source, while the S.A.S. itself is a resident entity-level taxpayer. Tax_Exempt_Zone: not applicable – the SPV is not located in a Zona Franca, and FTZ status would require separate DIAN authorization and the 20% reduced FTZ rate rather than an exemption.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Colombia. Statutory elections and mechanisms relevant to a pure equity holding S.A.S.: (a) optional accession to the Colombian Holding Company regime (Régimen de Compañías Holding Colombianas – CHC, introduced by Law 1943 of 2018, amended by Law 2010 of 2019 and implemented by Decree 1367 of 2020), requiring a minimum direct or indirect 10% interest in qualifying foreign companies, economic substance in Colombia (employees, assets and real local activity), and formal acceptance/registration with DIAN; the regime grants look-through treatment to qualifying foreign-source dividends and capital gains and treaty-eligible characterization; (b) for natural persons only, the 'no responsables' VAT simplification when prior-year gross income and bank deposits remain below 3,500 UVT; (c) mandatory rather than elective anti-hybrid rules: Colombian CFC attribution and the interest deduction limitation of Article 118-1 ET apply automatically and cannot be waived; (d) elective RUT status declarations allowing the SPV to reflect the CIIU/ISIC 6420 activity as 'actividad de tenencia' and to document the absence of any VAT responsibility; (e) no pass-through election is available for the S.A.S.; the entity is a hard-law corporate taxpayer.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia), acting jointly with the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) for supervision of foreign exchange intermediaries, under the statutory framework of Law 9 of 1991, Decree 1735 of 1993, and Resolution Externa No. 1 of 2020 (Board of Directors).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP) is convertible on the current account without prior licence; capital account flows, including inbound equity subscription into a S.A.S., outbound dividend distributions, and intragroup loan repatriation, must be executed exclusively through the 'mercado cambiario' (authorized foreign exchange market) and registered with Banco de la República via authorized local intermediaries. Foreign direct investment (FDI) enjoys free profit and dividend remittance for entities that complete the formal foreign investment registration (Registro de Inversión Supranacional and Formulario No. 6 / electronic registration through the FX dealers). No overall quantitative ceiling applies to convertibility, but capital transactions outside the permitted channels are illegal and settled using the representative market rate (TRM). Certain sectors (financial institutions, national media, hydrocarbon frontier areas) remain subject to special restrictions. The holding SPV's passive dividend model is legally viable for registration and conversion if share subscriptions are paid in foreign currency through authorized channels and the ultimate beneficial owner chain is declared.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Colombia does not impose a blanket mandatory conversion ratio on all exporters; however, export proceeds from goods must be channeled through the authorized foreign exchange market and reintegrated to a local account within a maximum of six (6) months after the maturity date of the related collection instrument and in no case later than eight (8) months after the date of shipment/boarding. The exporter must register the operation with the intermediary bank using the export declaration (Formulario Único de Exportación) and complete the applicable 'Declaración de Canalización' / reintegro de divisas. Foreign currency may be retained in duly registered external compensation accounts (cuentas de compensación) for lawful working-capital needs, but the use of unregistered offshore accounts for export collections is a compliance violation. For a pure equity holding SPV without export operations, these surrender rules are largely non-operative, although any incidental service income from subsidiaries must be classified correctly to avoid inadvertent non-compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.capital_account_registration_gate: Inbound FDI must be reported by the investor to the intermediary bank within the applicable statutory filing windows; registration must reflect the legal act (suscription of shares) and the actual disbursement trace, and the foreign investor will obtain a 'Registro de Inversiones Internacionales' certificate for future dividend and capital repatriation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.regulatory_reporting_calendar: The SPV and its shareholders must file Form 9/6 registrations, update beneficial-owner disclosures upon any share transfer, and present annual certification confirming the registered investment data.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.penalty_regime_for_forex_violations: Unauthorized foreign exchange transactions, late registrations, and misreported operation codes trigger fines by the SFC and exclusion of tax deductibility of the underlying cost, plus potential confiscation for unlawful currency evasion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account in COP plus Foreign Currency Compensation Account (USD and EUR)
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account in COP plus USD Nostro-Compensation Account
Operational Account in COP and Foreign Currency Compensation Account (USD, EUR, GBP)
Operational Account in COP plus Compensation Account in USD/EUR
Operational Account in COP and Foreign Currency Compensation Account (USD/CAD)
Operational Account in COP and Foreign Currency Compensation Account (USD/EUR)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Revolut, Airwallex, etc.) generally cannot serve as the primary treasury and clearing institution for this Colombian Pure Equity Holding SPV because Colombia's foreign exchange and capital-account regime requires all inbound investment, dividend repatriation, and credit operations to be conducted through locally authorized foreign-exchange intermediaries. A foreign EMI not licensed by the SFC cannot legally register the 'mercado cambiario' transactions, issue an acceptable compensation account, or provide the documentary signatures required by Banco de la República and DIAN. EMIs may be used only as down-stream execution agents after the primary Colombian clearing bank processes the FX registration, subject to heightened AML/KYC due diligence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The legal representative and at least one designated signatory of the S.A.S. must make a physical in-person appearance before the compliance officer and bank branch manager at the selected Colombian bank (or undertake a biometric video-identification session strictly accepted by the bank under its internal risk policy) to open the corporate account. Directors and ultimate beneficial owners may be interviewed remotely upon prior scheduling, but the final account activation for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced holding-SPV structure ordinarily requires physical signature on the account opening minutes and notarized powers-of-attorney. Remote-only opening is not accepted for this entity type by the tier-one banks referenced above.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ultimate beneficial-ownership chain or extraterritorial parent/share-holder structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed Beneficial Owner registry declaration (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales) under Resolution DIAN 164 of 2021; apostilled notarized power-of-attorney; authenticated corporate excerpt from the Cámara de Comercio showing the full share register and UBO cascade; foreign parent certificates of incorporation and the summarized ownership-chain chart showing each intermediate entity's jurisdiction, registration and legal status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic-substance deficiency of a passive pure-equity holding vehicle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bylaws of the S.A.S. expressly limiting the corporate purpose to ISIC 6420 (holding and administration of shares/equity interests); subsidiary board resolution confirming the existence of the SPV and its shareholding control; structural memoranda evidencing the group's commercial reasons for placing the SPV in Colombia; annual audited financial statements; transfer-pricing documentation (or a mark-to-market intercompany dividend projection); a factual economic-substance letter from the external auditor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds suspicion on the capital contribution wire
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements covering the last six months of the investor and its intermediate parents; signed loan agreements or dividend minutes evidencing lawful accumulation of funds; certified tax clearance receipts from the investor's residence jurisdiction (OECD CRS and FATCA self-certification forms, i.e. W-8BEN-E); the original SWIFT MT103 credit advice showing the matching reference number; notarized capital-contribution minutes of the S.A.S.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed person (PEP) or sanctions-list screening on the board or UBOs
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed PEP declarations in the bank's mandated form; negative sanctions screening results issued by a recognized sanctions-search provider (OFAC, UN, EU, and Colombian Listas Vinculantes); valid passports and residence proof of all signatories and UBOs; explanatory legal memorandum describing the holding SPV's asset custody chain and the absence of shell-vehicle risk indicators.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign investors must remit the equity subscription in USD/EUR via a direct SWIFT MT103 (or a Tier-1 correspondent MT202 for cover) to the S.A.S.'s authorized compensation account (cuenta de compensación en moneda extranjera) at the selected Colombian bank. The FLOW: (1) the bank receives the wire and matches the payment to the executed capital subscription minutes; (2) the bank officer prepares the 'Formulario No. 6 / Declaración de Cambio' coded as FDI in shares (Código 6011 or functionally equivalent); (3) the capital is converted to COP at the TRM upon the client's taxable instruction; (4) the pesos are credited to the S.A.S.'s operational account; and (5) the bank issues the 'Registro de Inversión Supranacional' registration certificate. All wires must contain the beneficiary S.A.S. NIT, reference clause to the nominative share subscription and date of the corporate minute, and the country of origin of the investor; incomplete purpose references cause a hold-up at the compensation account and trigger enhanced CDD.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury flows for the holding SPV consist primarily of: (i) dividend remittances to foreign shareholders, (ii) repayment of intragroup shareholder loans, and (iii) administrative service payments to the parent or affiliates. Clearing rails used are SWIFT MT103 for ordinary profit remittances; MT202 COV for interbank cover; and, where trade goods or services are financed by commercial letters of credit, SWIFT MT700/MT710 via the Colombian issuing bank's trade desk. Each outgoing transaction requires a Declaration of Change (Formulario de Declaración de Cambio, e.g., codes 7250 for dividend remittance) supported by minutes of the shareholders' meeting approving the dividend, certified tax payment receipts (dividends to non-residents are generally subject to Colombian tax of 35% for 2025 unless reduced by treaty or domestic legislation), the registered foreign investment certificate, and the invoice/contract for service payments. For the passive holding company, the use of unregistered foreign accounts or an offshore EMI to make the disbursement to shareholders is non-compliant and must be avoided; the full FX channel through the authorized Colombian intermediary bank remains mandatory.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC FX forwards on USD/COP and EUR/COP executed with locally authorized Colombian commercial banks (deliverable forwards tied to the TRM) for cash-flow hedging of the SPV's equity/investment and dividend flows

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on emerging-market currency pairs referencing the official TRM, used by foreign parent counterparties and Colombian banks to hedge COP exposure where physical delivery is impractical
Cross-currency swaps (USD/COP) and interest-rate swaps collateralized under ISDA/CSA documentation, reserved for hedging intragroup financing and long-dated dividend flows
Plain-vanilla FX options (EUR/USD and USD/COP) approved by the bank's treasury desk for protection against unfavorable TRM changes on capital repatriation

Money-market and time-deposit sweeps in COP at the local bank (CDTs) and foreign-currency deposits in authorized compensation accounts, used as liquidity buffers and not as speculative instruments; derivative hedging requires documented genuine underlying exposure and is prohibited for speculative trading by Colombian non-financial corporates

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial registration renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered office (local Chamber of Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January through 31 March; the renewal is calendar-year based, not anniversary based.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers an extemporaneous surcharge applied by the Chamber tariff, may produce loss of evidentiary standing of registered acts, and after three consecutive years of non-renewal the Chamber may initiate removal of the commercial registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of approved annual financial statements and management report (Estados Financieros e Informe de Gestión)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the domicile (commercial registration office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve the annual financial statements by 31 March; the signed statements and management report must be deposited with the Chamber within three months after approval (calendar-year companies in practice by 30 June).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-deposit or late deposit makes the financial statements ineffective against third parties, exposes the legal representative to Chamber fines, and may suspend access to certain commercial registry services.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual update of the Single Registry of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales – RUB)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the DIAN-published calendar; for calendar-year entities the RUB update generally closes in May following the fiscal year end; any share transfer made during the year is included in that annual confirmation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to timely update exposes the company to DIAN fines under the Estatuto Tributario and may restrict the evidentiary value of shareholding documentation in tax and administrative proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholders' annual meeting minute approving the financial statements (Acta de Asamblea de Accionistas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate statutory records; produced for inspection by the Chamber and DIAN; not individually filed unless the Chamber requests legalization
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March following the fiscal year end; meeting must be held and recorded before the financial statement deposit deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold and record the annual meeting by 31 March prevents lawful approval of the financial statements, constitutes breach of fiduciary duty by management, and may give shareholders grounds for liability action.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory auditor (revisor fiscal) becomes mandatory when the SAS has gross assets equal to or exceeding 5,000 monthly legal minimum wages (SMLMV) or gross revenue equal to or exceeding 3,000 SMLMV at the close of the preceding fiscal year; a below-threshold pure equity holding SPV is not required to appoint an auditor unless shareholders voluntarily decide one or a lender/consolidation group requires it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NIIF/IFRS as adopted in Colombia through DUR 2420 of 2015, with classification into Group 1 (full IFRS), Group 2 (IFRS for SMEs), or Group 3 (micro-entity NIIF); the applicable group is reassessed annually based on the entity's asset, employment, and revenue thresholds.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The legal representative must verify and annually confirm through the DIAN RUB portal the detailed ownership map of all natural persons who ultimately own or control 5% or more of the shares or voting power. Share transfers occurring during the year are aggregated and declared in the annual RUB update; in addition, each transfer must be recorded in the statutory shareholders' register as of the transaction date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro de Registro de Junta Directiva y Representantes Legales)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea de Accionistas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 – 900 per year for registered office address, municipal commercial registration support, and local compliance representation
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800 – 3,500 per year for a simple passive holding SPV when a statutory audit or revisor fiscal is required; voluntary review or compilation will be lower

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Dividends received from Colombian subsidiaries out of already-taxed profits are exempt income at the holding entity level. No general tax holiday applies to a pure equity holding SPV; sectoral incentives (e.g., new technology ventures, strategic industrial projects) are not ordinarily available to passive intermediate holding vehicles. Capital gains on share disposals are taxed as ordinary income unless a specific relief applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 210 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios) – filed electronically through DIAN's MUISCA e-filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due between 1 April and 10 May of the following taxable year, determined by the last two digits of the taxpayer's NIT (tax identification number). Payment of any outstanding tax is due on the same filing date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All revenue derived from commercial or operational activity. For a pure equity holding SPV, this is normally zero.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident parent does not file Form 210; the Colombian S.A.S. reports separately. No consolidation of foreign operational revenue is permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Covers dividends, participations, interest, royalties and other non-operating income. Dividends sourced from already-taxed Colombian subsidiary profits are treated as exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the Colombian SPV reports. The non-resident shareholder must not include Colombian-source dividends directly on its own Form 210; instead, the SPV reports the exempt portion and any taxable portion as required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All allowable costs and expenses, including interest expense, administrative overhead, professional fees, and depreciation, subject to the arm's length principle and thin-capitalisation rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent intercompany charges must be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; otherwise the deduction may be disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base computed as gross income minus deductions and exempt dividends. For an SPV with no operations and no taxable proceeds, this may be nil.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The calculation must be performed in Colombian pesos using DIAN-prescribed FX rates when foreign currency is involved; non-resident shareholders are not required to enter amounts here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The resulting income tax at the 35% statutory rate after applying credits, withholdings, and prepayments. Any final balance due or balance in favor is reported here.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholdings suffered on payments to the non-resident parent are not credited on this return unless the parent is the Colombian taxpayer. The withholding becomes a final tax at the shareholder level.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a monthly or fraction-of-month surcharge of 5% of the tax due, capped at 100% of the tax, plus monetary default interest (approximately 2.7% per month recalculated annually). Failure to file allows DIAN to issue a deemed assessment and may trigger an additional penalty of 1% of gross income. Late payment, understatement, or omission of income can lead to sanctions up to 160% of the evaded tax and criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends distributed from profits already subjected to Colombian corporate income tax; 35% on dividends distributed from untaxed profits or from profits qualifying as 'non-taxed reserves' at the distributing entity.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief on dividends, interest, or royalties, the non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home-country tax authority and deliver it, together with a completed sworn declaration confirming beneficial ownership and absence of treaty-abuse, to the Colombian withholding agent before payment. The withholding agent then applies the reduced treaty rate at source. Where excess withholding has occurred, the non-resident may obtain a refund through DIAN by filing an administrative refund claim (solicitud de devolución y/o compensación) and supporting documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rates are 15% for interest paid to non-residents and 20% for royalties/rentals paid abroad. Under applicable double tax agreements, rates may be reduced (interest typically 5%–10%, royalties 0%–20%) depending on the treaty and subject to TRC and limitation-on-benefits clauses.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: 100,000 UVT (approximately COP 4.7 billion for tax year 2024) of gross assets or gross income triggers mandatory Local File and Master File documentation for taxpayers with related-party transactions. A separate transfer pricing return is also required when transactions with related parties exceed 10,000 UVT.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not operate a formal offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations regime, but the tax administration applies a substance-over-form and general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR). A pure equity holding SPV must demonstrate real business purpose, minimum substance (board decisions, corporate records, local management/control), and economic rationale for all intercompany transactions. Lack of substance can trigger recharacterisation, disallowance of deductions, deemed dividends, and application of the CFC rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Return Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting taxable income, claiming false deductions, manipulating invoices, or filing Form 210 with materially incorrect data to reduce the Colombian corporate income tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of up to 160% of the evaded tax, default interest, business closure orders, and criminal prosecution under the Colombian Criminal Code (evasión fiscal) carrying imprisonment of 4 to 9 years and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or cause false returns to be filed may be jointly and severally liable for the tax, penalties, and interest; individual directors can face criminal imprisonment, travel bans, and asset attachment orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell Company Without Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a pure holding SPV with no physical presence, no employees, no bank account activity in Colombia, and no corporate administration in-country, used only to channel dividends and avoid tax in the parent jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may disregard the entity and recharacterize income at the shareholder level, deny dividend treaty benefits, apply deemed dividends, and levy sanctions equal to 160% of the assessed underpayment; the transaction structure may also be declared a sham.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for the underpaid tax under the GAAR, plus restrictions on leaving the country while tax proceedings are pending, and potential criminal liability for abuse of legal forms.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare, file, or maintain contemporaneous Local File/Master File documentation, or charging intercompany fees, interest, or royalties at prices departing from the arm's length principle without support.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of intercompany deductions, adjustment of taxable income, a penalty of up to 10,000 UVT for documentation failures, and a penalty of 5% of the transaction value for improper pricing; interest accrues on any additional assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve unsupported intercompany transactions may be jointly liable for the additional corporate tax and penalties; in egregious cases, criminal sanctions for aiding tax evasion can extend to imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Breach in Cross-Border Flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the holding SPV to receive high-risk cross-border wire transfers, distributing dividends to opaque structures without beneficial ownership disclosure, or conducting transactions with shell entities in non-transparent jurisdictions lacking substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines and asset forfeiture under Law 526/1999 and anti-money-laundering regulations; criminal money-laundering charges under the Colombian Criminal Code carry imprisonment of 10 to 20 years and monetary penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Company directors can be prosecuted as co-authors or accomplices if they allowed the entity to be used for laundering proceeds; banking relationships may be terminated, and personal travel bans and freezing of personal assets may be ordered by courts.
